Model controls and OpenCode session identity

The operator page is https://models.in.drlario.org. Detailed telemetry remains at Grafana. The page controls the owners directly; inference does not pass through it.

Fixed model selection

Choose a hardware-prefixed model in OpenCode. Its immutable ID fixes the weights, context, KV precision, slot count and preset. Selecting another profile loads it only when its hardware is idle. A busy device refuses a different profile; requests for the resident profile share its available slots. No cross-model queue or fallback to a different device is used.

Client context is server context minus 4096 tokens. Regular Geekom Smart's large capacity profile has 245760 server / 241664 client tokens, five slots and Q8 K/V. It is the default, rather than Flash Next. Dense Geekom slot counts remain provisional calculations; this rollout does not claim a throughput improvement.

Operator controls

Control Effect
Turn on Clear durable Off and start serving cold; inference loads a selected profile
Turn off Refuse busy inference or a hardware workload lock, then stop owned serving; Off survives reboot
Load when idle Preload that exact enabled profile; refuse busy, paused or Off hardware
Enable / Disable Permit/refuse new inference for a profile; disabling a busy device is refused
Cancel run Tombstone that registered run, disconnect its inference and request an exact-run OpenCode interruption
Cancel request Disconnect inference from a caller without trusted run control; do not claim its agent stopped
Cancel inference Cancel the snapshot of active inference and attempt registered run interruption; keep admission paused
Cancel and turn off Cancel tracked inference and stop owned serving; refuse another workload's hardware lock
Resume Reopen admission after cancellation; it does not override Off

Enable/disable controls admission; use Turn off to release the serving runtime. All mutations require a fresh owner revision and an idempotency key. A stale page refreshes rather than forcing a change. Offline/stale status is not proof that a device stopped. Controls are disabled after ten seconds without fresh data.

The current page covers chat/vision serving and their tracked inference requests. Image/encoder jobs retain their existing tools and hardware lock: the page refuses Off while they hold the device instead of falsely declaring it available. Intel service lifecycle and synchronous OpenVINO job cancellation are separate work. An idle/tool-running conversation is not an inference reservation and is not listed as an active inference request. Cancellation does not undo completed tool effects or kill arbitrary background processes or unrelated child conversations.

Identity and cancellation safety

Each development installation has a distinct inference key for each device. The owner derives the client from that authenticated key, never from a claimed hostname header. Existing shared role keys remain accepted for other callers but cannot establish registered OpenCode identity.

The v2 plugin attaches conversation ID, current user-message/run ID, plugin instance ID, conversation title, location and request kind. Titles and run metadata are visible only after operator login. Retries and tool continuations retain their run identity; a new user turn gets a different one. Primary, title, compaction and generation requests can be distinguished without logging content. Background title/generate requests have session identity but request-only cancellation, because they can overlap a newer user turn. Requests that began before plugin installation may lack run identity until a new explicit user turn. They remain usable and are labelled uninstrumented.

The page uses a dedicated SSH key with a forced command and forwarding disabled. machine-setup's helper accepts only exact-run control for an existing OpenCode session at its recorded location. It calls the supported plugin RPC; it neither edits OpenCode databases nor exposes OpenCode's general management API.

The plugin compares both current run and instance immediately before interruption. It places a synchronous cancellation barrier before awaiting OpenCode's interrupt with resume:false. New turns during that barrier are refused with a retry message. Stale run/instance actions cannot interrupt a newer turn. Conversations are preserved. The page reports interrupted, idle, stale_run, stopping, unsupported or unconfirmed, rather than treating network failure as success. Uninstrumented Hermes/other callers receive inference cancellation only. This rollout does not restart or resume the parked Hermes fleet.

Credentials, installation and recovery

The login username is lario. Retrieve the initial password privately on Bigcachy:

cat ~/.config/lario-model-control/operator-password

The non-root container receives only its operator hash, owner management keys, restricted SSH key and pinned known-hosts file. The browser receives none of those credentials. Login uses private server-side sessions, Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies, CSRF/origin checks and bounded failures. Sessions/audit state and owner policy live privately on XFS, outside Git. No prompts, responses or inference authorization headers are stored by the control page.

Source ownership:

  • lario-llms: shared/serving, fixed catalog/gateway, page, plugin and tests.
  • machine-setup: three client overlays, read-only model MCP, restricted helper.
  • lario-home-infra: private compose deployment, boot reconciliation and Caddy route.

Provisioning is repeatable and preserves existing private credentials:

cd ~/Projects/personal/lario-llms
python shared/serving/provision_control.py prepare
# After the updated owner gateways are running:
python shared/serving/provision_control.py install

The latter installs scoped keys only after all gateways accept them, installs the forced-command public key, renders client sources and reloads OpenCode. The plugin has no runtime dependency downloads. Its development API dependency is pinned to @opencode/plugin 2.0.22.

If the page fails, owner CLI remains available:

python shared/serving/control.py geekom status
python shared/serving/control.py geekom catalog
python shared/serving/control.py geekom activate --profile '<fixed-profile-id>'
python shared/serving/control.py rtx5080 off
python shared/serving/control.py rtx5080 on

CLI cancellation disconnects inference only; the page also invokes registered client run control. Repeated Off cannot be bypassed by reboot or a model request. Owners need not boot together: the page reconnects automatically when they return. Physical power-order testing is separate from this implementation.

Verification

tests/check_opencode_identity.py runs installed OpenCode against a disposable local fake model. It verifies actual identity headers, guarded interruption, new-turn identity and refusal of stale cancellation without GPU inference. test_fixed_serving.py, test_model_panel.py, test_model_client_control.py cover admission/reconciliation, credential identity, lifecycle contention, login/CSRF, truthful cancellation reporting and the restricted helper.

shared/serving/verify_control.py also checks the deployed container-to-client forced SSH command and stale-run guard on all three hosts with disposable idle sessions; it creates no model inference.

The plugin interfaces were checked against the installed package and official OpenCode v2 plugin hooks and plugin RPC documentation.
